introduction_md:
## Expressing Regret and Alternative Outcomes

En esta lección vas a aprender a expresar arrepentimiento sobre decisiones pasadas y a imaginar cómo habrían sido las cosas si hubieras actuado de otra manera. Este es un tema muy humano: todos hemos tomado decisiones de las que luego nos hemos arrepentido.

**¿Qué vas a lograr?**

- Expresar arrepentimiento usando **wish/if only + past perfect** (I wish I had...).
- Hipotetizar sobre resultados alternativos usando **would have** (It would have been better...).
- Usar vocabulario natural para hablar de decisiones: **settle for**, **go back on**, **give in**, **weigh up**.

**¿Por qué es importante?**

- Para conversaciones profundas sobre la vida y las decisiones.
- Para reflexionar sobre el pasado con matices, no solo con "I regret it".
- Para sonar más natural y sofisticado al hablar de experiencias personales.

**El escenario de hoy:**

Vas a seguir la historia de Marta, una profesional que aceptó un trabajo que no la convencía del todo. A lo largo de la lección, explorarás sus dudas, su arrepentimiento y las lecciones que aprendió. Este contexto te ayudará a practicar las estructuras en situaciones reales y memorables.

¡Empecemos!
intro_target:
## Expressing Regret and Alternative Outcomes

In this lesson, you will learn to express regret about past decisions and to imagine how things would have been if you had acted differently. This is a very human topic: we have all made decisions that we later regretted.

**What will you achieve?**

- Express regret using **wish/if only + past perfect** (I wish I had...).
- Hypothesise about alternative outcomes using **would have** (It would have been better...).
- Use natural vocabulary to talk about decisions: **settle for**, **go back on**, **give in**, **weigh up**.

**Why is it important?**

- For deep conversations about life and decisions.
- To reflect on the past with nuance, not just with "I regret it".
- To sound more natural and sophisticated when talking about personal experiences.

**Today's scenario:**

You will follow the story of Marta, a professional who accepted a job she was not entirely convinced about. Throughout the lesson, you will explore her doubts, her regret, and the lessons she learned. This context will help you practise the structures in real and memorable situations.

Let's get started!

grammar_explanations.slug: wish/if only + past perfect for regret
grammar_explanations.title_form: Arrepentimiento: wish / if only + past perfect
grammar_explanations.title_target: Regret: wish / if only + past perfect
grammar_explanations.description_md_form:
Para expresar **arrepentimiento** sobre decisiones pasadas, usamos `wish` o `if only` seguidos de **past perfect** (`had + participio`). Esta estructura indica que deseamos que el pasado hubiera sido diferente.

**Estructura:**

`I wish / If only + subject + had + past participle`

**Ejemplos:**

- `I wish I hadn't gone back on my promise.` (Ojalá no hubiera roto mi promesa.)
- `If only I hadn't settled for that job offer.` (Si solo no me hubiera conformado con esa oferta.)

**Significado:**

- `I wish I had...` = Desearía haber... (pero no lo hice).
- `I wish I hadn't...` = Desearía no haber... (pero lo hice).

**Forma negativa:** `hadn't + past participle`.

**Alternativas hipotéticas:**

Para hablar del **resultado alternativo** que imaginamos, usamos `would have + past participle` en la cláusula principal:

- `If only I had pulled off the negotiation, I wouldn't have had to turn down the offer.`
- `I wish I hadn't given in to pressure, because the outcome would have been different.`

**Nota:** `If only` es más enfático que `I wish`. Ambos son intercambiables en la mayoría de contextos.

**Uso en contexto:**

Esta estructura es común al reflexionar sobre **decisiones** laborales o personales, especialmente cuando queremos enfatizar el **arrepentimiento** y las **consecuencias hipotéticas** de nuestras acciones pasadas.
grammar_explanations.description_md_target:
To express **regret** about past decisions, we use `wish` or `if only` followed by the **past perfect** (`had + past participle`). This structure indicates that we wish the past had been different.

**Structure:**

`I wish / If only + subject + had + past participle`

**Examples:**

- `I wish I hadn't gone back on my promise.`
- `If only I hadn't settled for that job offer.`

**Meaning:**

- `I wish I had...` = I regret not doing...
- `I wish I hadn't...` = I regret doing...

**Negative form:** `hadn't + past participle`.

**Alternative outcomes:**

To talk about the **hypothetical result**, we use `would have + past participle` in the main clause:

- `If only I had pulled off the negotiation, I wouldn't have had to turn down the offer.`
- `I wish I hadn't given in to pressure, because the outcome would have been different.`

**Note:** `If only` is more emphatic than `I wish`. Both are interchangeable in most contexts.

**Use in context:**

This structure is common when reflecting on **decisions** in work or personal life, especially when we want to emphasize **regret** and the **hypothetical consequences** of our past actions.

callouts.text_md: **`If only` es más enfático que `I wish`.** Úsalo cuando el arrepentimiento es muy fuerte o dramático. Ambos son correctos, pero `if only` añade carga emocional.
**No uses `would have` después de `wish`.** Decimos `I wish I had done...`, NUNCA `I wish I would have done...`. La forma correcta siempre usa `had + participio`.
**Cuidado con la doble negación.** `I wish I hadn't never...` es incorrecto. Usa solo una negación: `I wish I hadn't...` o `I wish I had never...`.

common_errors_es: Usar 'would have' después de 'wish': ✗ 'I wish I would have studied.' → ✓ 'I wish I had studied.'
Olvidar el past perfect y usar pasado simple: ✗ 'I wish I didn't go.' → ✓ 'I wish I hadn't gone.'
Confundir 'if only' con 'only if': 'if only' expresa deseo/arrepentimiento; 'only if' expresa condición exclusiva.
Traducir literalmente 'ojalá' como 'I hope': para arrepentimiento usamos 'I wish' o 'if only', no 'I hope'.

exercises.passage_md: Looking back, I realize I made a terrible mistake when I decided to go back on my word. My colleague had worked hard on a project, and I had promised to support her decision to present it to the board. However, under pressure from my manager, I gave in and turned down her proposal. The outcome was disastrous for her career, and our work relationship never recovered. In hindsight, I wish I had pulled off the courage to stand by her. If only I had weighed up the consequences more carefully, I would have realized that her idea was actually brilliant. I settled for an easy path, and that decision cost me a valuable friendship. Now, whenever I face a similar situation, I try to remember that going back on a promise is never worth it. The regret I feel is a constant reminder that integrity matters more than temporary approval.

exercises.passage_md: The company's decision to go back on its promise to invest in new technology had a significant impact. The employees had been excited about the project, but when the management gave in to financial pressure and turned down the proposal, morale dropped. Many talented workers decided to leave, and the company struggled to recover. In hindsight, the leaders wished they had weighed up the long-term benefits of the investment. If only they had considered the potential outcome, they would have realized that saving money in the short term was not worth losing their best people. The regret was clear in their annual report, where they admitted that settling for immediate profits was a mistake. The experience taught them a valuable lesson about the importance of commitment and foresight.

exercises.prompt_md: Leé el texto y respondé: ¿Qué consejo le daría el autor a alguien que está por tomar una decisión difícil?

exercises.explanation_md: El autor aconseja 'do not let fear make the decision for you', lo que significa que no se debe actuar por miedo.
exercises.passage_md: I remember a time when I had to choose between two paths. One was safe and predictable, the other was risky but potentially rewarding. I chose the safe one, and I have regretted it ever since. I settled for comfort instead of chasing my dreams. In hindsight, I wish I had been braver. If only I had listened to my heart rather than my fears. The outcome of my decision was not terrible, but it was not fulfilling either. I learned that going back on your own aspirations is the worst kind of betrayal. My advice is simple: weigh up the risks, but do not let fear make the decision for you. The regret of not trying is often harder to bear than the regret of failing.

questions.passage_md: Looking back on that period of my life, I can't help but feel a profound sense of responsibility for the outcome. We had a clear agreement, a verbal contract that seemed solid enough at the time. My partner, a man of principle, had trusted my judgment completely. He had turned down a more lucrative offer from a competitor because I had convinced him that our joint venture would succeed. I had promised him that we would pull it off, that our combined expertise would guarantee a positive result. However, when the market shifted unexpectedly, I panicked. Instead of standing firm, I chose to go back on my word. I settled for a compromise that I knew was far below what we had originally envisioned. I told myself it was a strategic retreat, but deep down, I knew it was a betrayal of his trust. The decision was not just a professional failure; it was a personal one. If only I had been more patient, if only I had had the courage to wait for a better opportunity, the outcome might have been entirely different. His disappointment was palpable, and it was a direct consequence of my actions. I had given in to fear, and that single moment of weakness defined the end of our partnership. The regret is not about the money we lost; it's about the relationship I destroyed through my inability to stay true to my commitments.

questions.passage_md: The negotiation had been long and exhausting. For weeks, we had been trying to reach a consensus with the other company. They had made an initial offer that was frankly insulting, and we had rejected it outright. We knew our product was superior, and we were confident that they would eventually come around. However, as the deadline approached, my colleague began to waver. He argued that a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush, and that we should accept their second offer, even though it was still below our minimum target. I disagreed strongly. I felt that if we held out a little longer, we could get a much better deal. I had seen this tactic work before, and I was sure that they were bluffing. I told him not to give in, that we had the upper hand. But he was tired and anxious about the future of the company. In the end, he went behind my back and accepted their terms. He settled for an outcome that I considered a failure. I was furious, not just because of the financial loss, but because he had gone back on our agreement to stand firm. I felt betrayed. If only he had trusted my judgment, we could have achieved a far more favorable result. That experience taught me a valuable lesson about the importance of having partners who share your vision and your nerve.

notes_md_form:
## Errores comunes con 'wish' + past perfect

Para hispanohablantes, lo mas dificil es recordar que en inglés usamos **past perfect** (had + participio) despues de 'wish' o 'if only' para hablar de arrepentimientos del pasado. No digas 'I wish I didn't go back on my word' si la accion ya ocurrio y no puedes cambiarla. Lo correcto es: **'I wish I hadn't gone back on my word'**. El truco: piensa en 'habia hecho' en español, no en 'hice'.

## Conecta con tu vida real

Piensa en una decision que tomaste y que ahora ves de otra forma. Por ejemplo: 'I wish I hadn't settled for that job offer' o 'If only I had tried out that other option'. Usa estos patrones para hablar de tus propias experiencias. Nota que con 'would have' expresas el resultado alternativo: 'If I had waited, things would have worked out better'. Practica con tus decisiones reales: es la forma mas rápida de interiorizar la estructura.
